table.title: [Swatow Harbour: particulars]
table.caption_extra: Section: River Conservancy and Harbours. Swatow Harbour — Work Done

rows: The Swatow Bar is situated half way between Bill Island and Sugarloaf. At high water, ordinary spring tides, this bar may be crossed by a ship drawing 21 feet 6 inches, with a pilot in charge, and the least water, in the fairway, at low water, is 15 feet, but great caution has to be exercised when there is a swell on.

There are in Swatow Harbour six pontoons, connected to the bund with bridges, they are, however, privately owned (4 Messrs. Butterfield and Swire, 1 Messrs. Jardine, and 1 the China Merchants) and only used by the Company's ships.
Number and size of vessels that can be accommodated
Room for about 30 vessels of ordinary coasting type.
Loading and unloading capacity per day
6 at pontoons and 12 mooring buoys, total 18 berths.
Sufficient bunker coal always in stock.
Pilotage not compulsory. Charge: $5.50 per foot draught plus 1 cent per ton over 1200 tons. Night charge $25.00 extra.
Pilots charge for shifting a vessel inside Harbour Limit, in stream $15.00, to or from pontoon $20.00, to or from Oil Installation vessels up to and including 1500 tons $15.00, over 1500 tons $25.00.

transcriber_notes: Run-in headed particulars (italic headings) transcribed as a list-table per brief. 'Number of berths': 6 + 12 = 18 — reconciles with printed total 18.
